html.p: The Timeline dataType renders a horizontal Gantt-style chart where each row is a named entity (machine, process, operator) and each coloured rectangle is a timed event. Activate it with dataType=Timeline.

The visualization handles axis construction, legend creation, colour assignment, and event rendering automatically. You only supply the search data and, optionally, an option string to customise the tooltip, grid layout, or dataZoom.
The search must return these columns in order:

tr.td: Event start — Unix timestamp in seconds
Event end — Unix timestamp in seconds
Optional — hex/rgb colour; omit when using timeline_useSplunkCategoricalColors=true

html.p: Timestamps must be Unix seconds (not milliseconds). Splunk functions now(), relative_time(), and strptime() all return seconds. The visualization multiplies them by 1000 internally for ECharts.

tr.td: Auto-assigns one Splunk palette colour per unique category value
Reads colour from the 5th column. Falls back to palette for rows with an empty/invalid colour

html.p: The search below simulates a production shift monitor for four machines: CNC-01, CNC-02, Conveyor-01, and Press-01. Each machine transitions between Running, Idle, Maintenance, and Error states throughout the shift. The base time is anchored to 8 hours before the current hour so the chart always shows the most recent shift window.

html.p: Key points about the option string for Timeline:

ul.li: xAxis, yAxis, series, and legend are built automatically — do not define them in the option unless you need to override defaults.
Add dataZoom to enable panning and zooming along the time axis.
Add grid to adjust margins. The left value controls the space for y-axis machine labels — increase it for longer names.
The tooltip formatter receives a params.data object with name (category), value[2] (internal_name), value[7] (unix start in seconds), value[8] (unix end in seconds), and eventDurationInSeconds.

html.p: To control colours precisely, set timeline_useSplunkCategoricalColors=false and provide a fill_color fifth column with a valid hex or rgb value per row. Rows with an empty or invalid colour fall back to the Splunk categorical palette automatically.

pre.code: | eval fill_color=case( state="Running", "#5cb85c", state="Idle", "#f0ad4e", state="Maintenance", "#337ab7", state="Error", "#d9534f", 1=1, "" ) | table start_time end_time machine state fill_color

html.p: Setting timeline_splitByHour=true changes the layout: the y-axis becomes hourly time slots and each machine's events are drawn as bars within those slots. This lets you see — for each hour of the shift — which machines were active, idle, or in maintenance, all on the same chart.

ul.li: The dashboard must be a <form> with a time-range picker using token="time_range" (this page already has one — use the picker at the top).
The search element must bind <earliest>$time_range.earliest$</earliest> and <latest>$time_range.latest$</latest>. The builder reads the time_range token name specifically.
Maximum supported range is 24 hours. Wider ranges produce a warning.

html.p: The chart below works with the existing renderer without any JavaScript changes. It creates a full-hour baseline event for each row, then overlays later state changes inside selected hours. Keep the picker at 24 hours or less; the default range shows the last eight complete hours.

search.query: | makeresults | addinfo | eval range_start=case(isnum(info_min_time) AND info_min_time>0, relative_time(info_min_time, "@h"), 1=1, relative_time(now(), "-8h@h")) | eval range_end=case(isnum(info_max_time) AND info_max_time<=now(), relative_time(info_max_time, "@h"), 1=1, relative_time(now(), "@h")) | eval range_end=if(range_end<=range_start, range_start+3600, range_end) | eval hour_count=ceil((range_end-range_start)/3600) | eval hour_count=if(hour_count>24, 24, hour_count) | eval hour_index=mvrange(0, hour_count) | mvexpand hour_index | eval hour_start=range_start+(hour_index*3600), machine="Packaging-01" | eval segment=mvappend("Running,0,60,0", if(hour_index=2,"Maintenance,20,60,1",""), if(hour_index=4,"Idle,35,60,1",""), if(hour_index=6,"Error,5,53,1",""), if(hour_index=6,"Running,53,60,2","")) | mvexpand segment | where segment!="" | eval parts=split(segment,",") | eval state=mvindex(parts,0), start_min=tonumber(mvindex(parts,1)), end_min=tonumber(mvindex(parts,2)), draw_order=tonumber(mvindex(parts,3)) | eval start_second=start_min*60, end_second=end_min*60 | eval start_time=hour_start+(start_min*60), end_time=hour_start+(end_min*60) | where end_time>start_time | sort 0 hour_index draw_order | table start_time end_time machine state hour_index start_second end_second

html.p: Full viz source for the chart above (copy into a <panel> of your own dashboard):

pre.code:
<viz type="visualization_toolbox.hman">
        <search>
          <query>| makeresults
| addinfo
| eval range_start=case(isnum(info_min_time) AND info_min_time>0, relative_time(info_min_time, "@h"), 1=1, relative_time(now(), "-8h@h"))
| eval range_end=case(isnum(info_max_time) AND info_max_time<=now(), relative_time(info_max_time, "@h"), 1=1, relative_time(now(), "@h"))
| eval range_end=if(range_end<=range_start, range_start+3600, range_end)
| eval hour_count=ceil((range_end-range_start)/3600)
| eval hour_count=if(hour_count>24, 24, hour_count)
| eval hour_index=mvrange(0, hour_count)
| mvexpand hour_index
| eval hour_start=range_start+(hour_index*3600), machine="Packaging-01"
| eval segment=mvappend("Running,0,60,0", if(hour_index=2,"Maintenance,20,60,1",""), if(hour_index=4,"Idle,35,60,1",""), if(hour_index=6,"Error,5,53,1",""), if(hour_index=6,"Running,53,60,2",""))
| mvexpand segment
| where segment!=""
| eval parts=split(segment,",")
| eval state=mvindex(parts,0), start_min=tonumber(mvindex(parts,1)), end_min=tonumber(mvindex(parts,2)), draw_order=tonumber(mvindex(parts,3))
| eval start_second=start_min*60, end_second=end_min*60
| eval start_time=hour_start+(start_min*60), end_time=hour_start+(end_min*60)
| where end_time>start_time
| sort 0 hour_index draw_order
| table start_time end_time machine state hour_index start_second end_second</query>
          <earliest>$time_range.earliest$</earliest>
          <latest>$time_range.latest$</latest>
        </search>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.dataType">Timeline</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.timeline_useSplunkCategoricalColors">true</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.timeline_splitByHour">true</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.timeline_bandHeight">32</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.timeline_bandGap">8</option>
        <option name="visualization_toolbox.hman.option">
option = {
  title: {
    text: 'Production Shift - Split by Hour',
    subtext: 'XML-only example: full-hour baseline events with ordered state overlays',
    left: 'center'
  },
  tooltip: {
    trigger: 'item',
    formatter: function (params) {
      var d = params.data;
      var durMin = Math.floor(d.eventDurationInSeconds / 60);
      var durSec = d.eventDurationInSeconds % 60;
      var dur = durMin > 0 ? durMin + ' min ' + durSec + ' s' : durSec + ' s';
      var start = new Date(d.value[10] * 1000).toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
      var end = new Date(d.value[11] * 1000).toLocaleTimeString([], { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit' });
      return d.value[2] + ' - ' + d.name + ' | ' + start + '-' + end + ' | ' + dur;
    }
  },
  toolbox: {
    feature: {
      dataZoom: { yAxisIndex: 'none', title: { zoom: 'Zoom', back: 'Reset zoom' } },
      restore:  { title: 'Reset' },
      saveAsImage: { title: 'Save' }
    }
  },
  grid: {
    left: 80,
    right: 60,
    bottom: 60
  },
  series: [
    {
      encode: {
        x: ['start_second', 'end_second'],
        y: 'hour_index'
      },
      renderItem: function (params, api) {
        var bandHeight = 32;
        var yIndex = api.value(4);
        var start = api.coord([api.value(5), yIndex]);
        var end = api.coord([api.value(6), yIndex]);
        return {
          type: 'rect',
          shape: {
            x: start[0],
            y: start[1] - bandHeight / 2,
            width: end[0] - start[0],
            height: bandHeight
          },
          style: api.style({
            fill: api.visual('color')
          })
        };
      }
    }
  ]
};
        </option>
        <option name="height">680</option>
        <option name="refresh.display">progressbar</option>
      </viz>

html.p: Two options control the visual density of the timeline:

tr.td: Height in pixels of each event rectangle
Vertical gap in pixels between rows

html.p: The chart canvas height is automatically computed as (bandHeight + bandGap) * numberOfRows + gridTop + gridBottom. Set the Splunk panel height option generously (e.g. 600) to ensure the full chart is visible without a scrollbar appearing inside the panel.
